input_article:
# The Notification You Hear Without Looking

A phone does not need to light up in your hand to change a task. A sound may be enough. And in another study, even a silent phone on a desk was linked to lower attention.

A study by Upshaw, Stevens, Ganis, and Zabelina, published in PLOS ONE on November 17, 2022, tested 73 college students. They worked through a letter task for 960 trials. In some trials, they heard a notification sound. In others, they heard a neutral sound. They did not look at or touch a phone.

The result was clear: responses were slower during trials with notification sounds. Brain recordings also showed a larger signal after those sounds. This happened even though the students kept working and did not check a screen.

A second study by Skowronek, Seifert, and Lindberg was published in Scientific Reports on June 8, 2023. It tested 42 university students. Their phones were powered off, and no notifications arrived. The researchers compared a phone on the desk with a phone in another room.

Performance was lower when the phone stayed on the desk. The attention score averaged 99.71 on the desk, compared with 108.95 when the phone was away. Processing speed was 98.48 on the desk and 108.57 in another room.

Together, these studies show two different moments. A notification can affect a person during a task. A phone can also be linked to lower performance without making a sound.

### The cost you cannot see

Distraction is not always a visible choice. Someone can keep working and still spend more effort to stay with the task. The researchers read the slower responses and larger brain signal as a sign of that extra control. So a person who never checks the screen may still pay an attention cost.

### Muting is not the same as absence

A silent phone is not the same as no phone. The second study suggests that silencing alerts and moving the device may address different problems, although it did not test either action as a solution. The social side matters too: 72% of U.S. teens often or sometimes checked messages or notifications soon after waking. And 56% reported at least one of anxiety, loneliness, or upset when their phone was not nearby.

## In one line…

These studies suggest a quiet lesson: attention can be pulled by a sound, or shared with a phone that never rings.

baseline.label: Baseline(既存方式Cのまま、追加ルールなし)

ledger_deviations.claim_in_article: Distraction is not always a visible choice.
ledger_deviations.issue: 通知音による注意捕捉や追加の認知制御努力は研究者の解釈であり、直接測定された事実そのものではないが、ここでは一般的な事実のように述べている。文自体は既確認の状況を会話的に導入するHookとして扱い、changed_scopeは緩和した。
ledger_deviations.explanation: F-003の著者解釈を明示的な帰属なしに断定調で提示しているため、changed_certaintyのみ該当。

ledger_deviations.claim_in_article: Someone can keep working and still spend more effort to stay with the task.
ledger_deviations.issue: 課題中に反応が遅れ、N2振幅が増大したことから追加の認知制御努力を要したという点は研究者の解釈であり、直接測定された「努力」ではない。また、実験参加者・実験課題の結果を一般の人に広げている。
ledger_deviations.explanation: F-002/F-003の解釈を一般的な事実として述べ、実験範囲を超えて一般化しているため。

A.label: Pattern A: Representative Metric + Supporting Trend

ledger_deviations.claim_in_article: These studies suggest a quiet lesson: attention can be pulled by a sound, or shared with a phone that never rings.
ledger_deviations.issue: F-007が確認しているのは、実験中に電源オフのスマートフォンへ通知が届かなかったことです。「never rings」は、実験期間内の条件を無期限の事実へ広げています。
ledger_deviations.explanation: 結論のHookとして、既存の「音が鳴らない／通知を受信しない」条件を会話的に言い換えた点は許容します。ただしHookでもcertaintyとtimeは緩和されないため、実験中に限られた不在を「never」とした点を軽微な過剰断定として記録します。

B.label: Pattern B: Conclusion-First / Numeric Necessity Test

ledger_deviations.claim_in_article: So a person who never checks the screen may still pay an attention cost.
ledger_deviations.issue: 実験で確認されたのは、参加者が課題中にスマートフォンを見たり触ったりしなかった条件での反応遅延であり、「画面を決して確認しない人」一般についての結果ではない。また、注意コストの解釈は研究者の解釈である。結論的なHookとしてchanged_scopeの緩和は適用するが、特定条件下の結果を一般的な人物について述べる点はchanged_certaintyとして残る。
ledger_deviations.explanation: 「may」で断定は弱められているものの、実験参加者・課題中の条件に限定された研究者の解釈を、画面を決して確認しない人一般への主張に広げている。Hookのためchanged_scopeは緩和したが、certaintyは通常通り判定した。
